components.text: Explain why evolution can yield abstract reasoning despite selection for practical capacities.
Account for the reliability limits expected when cognition is extended beyond its evolved domain.
Explain how evolved practical cognition can extend to abstraction while retaining expected limitations.
Account for human difficulty in domains far removed from ancestral selection pressures.
Explain how deduction preserves semantic relations rather than being mere physical succession.
Explain why logical validity and necessary entailment remain available under naturalism.
Explain how deductive transitions can preserve and respond to semantic or logical content under naturalism.
Show why objective deductive validity is insufficient for a person's deductive knowledge.
Distinguish truth of premises and recognition of entailment from validity alone.
Address whether necessary validity and semantic equivalence suffice for deductive knowledge by a reasoner.
Distinguish a rationally recognized entailment from conviction produced by causal succession alone.
Challenge the inference from non-intentional physical parts to a non-intentional whole.
Provide an example of a physical whole representing despite non-representing constituent atoms.
Answer the inference from non-intentional physical constituents to the representational insufficiency of their organized whole.
Show why artifact representation cannot explain original intentionality in human thought.
Identify the intentional maker or user presupposed by books, code, and computer outputs.
Determine whether the book counterexample explains original representation or presupposes intentional makers and interpreters.
Explain why survival selection favors capacities that reliably represent the environment.
Connect environmental tracking with investigation, classification, and rational inference.
Explain why survival-oriented selection would favor capacities that reliably investigate and classify environmental reality.
Connect practical environmental tracking with later rational inference and abstract extension.
Reject any inference from present naturalistic incompleteness directly to supernatural agency.
Preserve the requirement for an actual comparison of explanatory expectations.
Distinguish an unexplained intentionality gap from affirmative evidence for a supernatural cause.
Replace an inference from naturalistic incompleteness with a comparative evidential demand between naturalist and non-naturalist explanations.
Assess whether an unexplained naturalistic gap itself warrants supernatural or non-natural agency.
Supply a naturalistic continuity narrative for the development of conscious rational capacities.
Connect increasing awareness and abstract thought without invoking an abrupt non-natural intervention.
Provide a naturalistic continuity account from simple responsiveness to awareness and increasingly abstract mentality.
Explain how increasingly complex capacities could include abstract thought rather than only behavioral response.
Explain why a graded complexity narrative does not account for subjective perspective.
Address whether physical causal closure makes consciousness unnecessary to explain behavior.
Determine whether a gradient of functional complexity explains the presence of first-person subjective experience.
Explain what causal work consciousness performs if physical causes already suffice for behavior.
Answer the claim that consciousness would be evolutionarily or causally unnecessary.
Explain whether consciousness may be adaptive or a harmless evolutionary byproduct.
Show why byproduct status does not undermine the accuracy of reasoning.
Answer why consciousness exists under evolution if it is either causally useful or a causally harmless byproduct.
Address whether a byproduct origin undermines the accuracy of the resulting reasoning capacities.
Apply comparative expectedness to the observed development of conscious rational creatures.
Challenge the claimed comparative advantage of mentality-fundamental views using gradual development.
Account for long trial-and-error development and intermediate capacities under naturalism.
Compare how expected the observed gradual, trial-dependent development is under naturalism and non-natural agency.
Use the observed evolutionary trajectory as evidence bearing on the competing consciousness explanations.
Test whether mentality being fundamental predicts the particular developmental mechanism observed.
Challenge the inference from gradually increasing brain complexity to expected conscious awareness.
Distinguish sophisticated adaptive behavior from first-person subjective experience.
Question why consciousness accompanies behavior if physical causes are sufficient.
Determine whether gradual growth in neural and behavioral complexity predicts accompanying first-person awareness under naturalism.
Distinguish a graded functional trajectory from an explanation of subjective experience.
Assess whether compatibility as adaptation or byproduct supplies a positive expectation of awareness.
